steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Common separable prefixes: an-, aus-, auf-, ein-, mit-, nach-, vor-, zu-, zurück-, zusammen-, weg-. In subordinate clauses, the prefix stays attached: "...weil ich um 8 Uhr anfange" (NOT anfange ich).

steps.title: Exam Tip
steps.body: "Ich möchte" is technically the subjunctive of mögen but functions as a modal verb. It is the standard way to express "I would like" in German. Note: ich kann, ich muss, ich darf, ich will, ich soll — these all have NO -e ending in the ich form.

steps.title: German Exam Tips — Separable and Modal Verbs
steps.body: 1. For Separable and Modal Verbs, use a range of vocabulary and complex grammatical structures to access higher marks 2. Check verb tenses, agreements and word order carefully in your written work 3. In translation tasks, translate meaning rather than word-for-word 4. When writing about Separable and Modal Verbs, include opinions and justifications, not just descriptions 5. For listening and reading, focus on key words and cognates to extract meaning

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Rewrite with correct word order: Ich (einkaufen / gehen / am Samstag). | Q: Translate: I must do my homework. I would like to go to the cinema.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Ich gehe am Samstag einkaufen. (The separable prefix "ein-" goes to the END of the clause: ich gehe... ein.) | Ich muss meine Hausaufgaben machen. (Modal + infinitive at end.) Ich möchte ins Kino gehen. (Modal + infinitive at end.)

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Use a range of tenses (present, past, future) to access higher marks Include opinions with reasons (ich finde... weil... / meiner Meinung nach...) Check case endings (nominative, accusative, dative) before finishing Get word order right: verb-second in main clauses, verb-at-end after dass/weil/wenn Use complex structures: subordinate clauses, modal verbs, separable verbs Include cultural references to German-speaking countries (DACH)
